note: Free type system — the only fonts allowed on screen. 123 families are SIL OFL 1.1; Permanent Marker is Apache-2.0 (Font Diner) and Ubuntu is Ubuntu Font Licence 1.0 (Canonical) — see each family's licence/licence_file. The agent chooses the most fitting face per scene/element (plan/text-direction.json); there is no creative default. `fallback` is a last-resort safety net for system chrome only. `status`: ok = passes the shaping/collision gate (ratio < 0.20, see tests/test_fonts.py); review = measured >= 0.20 on 2026-11-09 — still usable deliberately for texture, but not offered as a starting point (see docs/fonts.md 'quarantine' and medo-motion/looks/shortlist.json).

Cairo.role: available option / system-chrome fallback — captions, body, lower thirds (not a forced creative default)

Tajawal.role: geometric headlines and numbers — short, confident lines

IBM Plex Sans Arabic.role: technical / UI / telemetry — label pairs, stat rows, device screens

Almarai.role: small captions and long body where legibility beats personality

Alexandria.role: big display Arabic (hook word, key number) — wide, modern, high impact

Kufam.role: kufic-geometric statement — chapter cards, poster-like frames, big numbers

El Messiri.role: Egyptian-flavoured modern display — titles with character, warm not corporate

Amiri.role: naskh serif — quotes, citations, a serious editorial beat

Rubik.role: rounded modern Arabic+Latin — friendly hooks, social captions, bold numbers

Changa.role: condensed Arabic display — punchy headlines, tight kinetic type, countdowns

Readex Pro.role: clean contemporary Arabic+Latin — readable body/UI with a modern edge

Lalezar.role: bold display statement — poster frames, chapter cards, big Arabic keywords

Inter.role: available option / system-chrome fallback — UI, data, mixed Arabic+Latin lines

Space Grotesk.role: technical display — product names, headers with an engineered edge

IBM Plex Sans.role: Latin half of the Plex superfamily — pairs 1:1 with IBM Plex Sans Arabic

IBM Plex Mono.role: code, specs, numbers that must line up — terminal / telemetry looks

Anton.role: one heavy display weight — hooks, single big numbers, CTA

Instrument Serif.role: editorial serif — quotes and pull-outs against the sans default

Archivo Black.role: heavy grotesque — loud hooks, single big numbers, stamp-like CTAs

Bebas Neue.role: tall condensed caps — trailer-style titles, countdowns, kinetic labels

Sora.role: geometric modern Latin — product/UI headers paired with rounded Arabic
